newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Nedlloyd Q1 loss deepens, sees profit for 97.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nedlloyd Q1 loss deepens, sees profit for 97.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd on Wednesday announced a trebling of first quarter losses, but forecast a profit on ordinary activities for the full year with faster than expected savings from its P&O Nedlloyd joint venture.

Nedlloyd's net losses from ordinary activties fell to 45 million guilders ($23.9 million), from 15 million in the first quarter last year. However, 1996's figure included a 30 million guilder capital gain on the sale of vessels, without which losses would have been the same.
The result was at the bottom end of analyst forecasts and well below the consensus 17 million guilder loss.

Shares in Nedlloyd, which have gained over 10 percent in a week, equalled a two month high of 50.30 guilders on Wednesday morning ahead of the results, but subsided to 48.20 guilders, 60 cents down on the day, by 1335 GMT.

The loss was the result of a weak performance in ocean shipping, hit by eight percent year-on-year tariff erosion. Nedlloyd's share in the P&O Nedlloyd first quarter loss was 38 million guilders, compared with a 33 million loss (excluding capital gains) in its Ocean Shipping division a year earlier.
But cost savings in this sector were expected to ensure profits for the whole of 1997.

"Based on our current knowledge...we expect Nedlloyd as a whole to achieve a positive result on ordinary activities in 1997," the company said in a statement with the results, although it said it was too early to give a specific projection.

The savings are to be realised in the company's P&O Nedlloyd joint venture with Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co. Nedlloyd said it expected the joint venture to contribute positively during 1997.

"Progress is ahead of schedule for merging the previous businesses into the new company. On an annualised basis, savings of $200 million will be achieved by Q4 1997," P&O Nedlloyd said in a statement issued at the same time as the Nedlloyd results.
"Merger costs will fall largely in Q2-Q4 1997 with synergy savings increasing through 1997 and into 1998. Total annual synergy will comfortably exceed the $200 million originally forecast," it added.
Excluding ocean shipping, the group made a profit of 13 million guilders, up from 10 million. Net turnover moved ahead to 851 million guilders from 804 million.
Analysts mostly agreed that the size of the losses was a surprise, agreed a turnaround in container shipping provided the key to profitability for the full year, but were mixed on the prospects.

"(Profits) were clearly at the bottom end of the range, but they expect savings to be higher. In such a cyclical industry, it's quite a brave statement...I think they will probably manage it," said Pieter van Gelder of Delta Lloyd Bank.
"It's a positive view, but we don't share that view. (Shipping) capacity will increase substantially and world trade growth will not keep up," said Oscar Poos of Paribas Capital Markets.
